summary: Inference-time LLM optimization can cut API spend by 40-95% while often improving latency, with no model retraining required. The highest-leverage techniques are prompt caching (up to 90% input discount), semantic caching (60-70% hit rates), model cascading/routing, and prompt compression. Combining a few of these typically takes monthly costs down by 80% or more without sacrificing output quality.

techniques.name: Prompt Caching
techniques.description: Reuses precomputed KV tensors for repeated prompt prefixes (system prompts, few-shot examples, documents), so the cached portion is billed at a steep discount and skips recomputation.
techniques.savings: up to 90% reduction on cached input tokens
techniques.example: Place your large static system prompt and few-shot examples at the start of every request so Anthropic/OpenAI caches the prefix; only the variable user question is charged at full price.

techniques.name: Semantic Caching
techniques.description: Caches LLM responses keyed by embedding similarity rather than exact string match, returning a stored answer when a new query is semantically close to a previous one.
techniques.example: Use GPTCache or Redis semantic cache so that 'How do I reset my password?' and 'password reset steps?' hit the same cached response instead of two API calls.

techniques.name: Model Cascading / Routing
techniques.description: Routes each request to the cheapest model capable of handling it, escalating to a larger model only when the small model's confidence or answer is insufficient.
techniques.example: Send all queries to GPT-4o-mini first and only escalate to GPT-4o when a validation check or confidence score indicates the cheap model failed.

techniques.name: Prompt Compression / Minimization
techniques.description: Removes redundant tokens, trims verbose instructions, and compresses context (e.g., with LLMLingua) to reduce input token count while preserving meaning.
techniques.example: Run long retrieved documents through LLMLingua to compress a 2,000-token context down to ~600 tokens before sending it to the model.

techniques.name: Output Token Limiting
techniques.description: Constrains response length via max_tokens and instructions to request concise or structured output, since output tokens are typically 2-4x more expensive than input tokens.
techniques.example: Set max_tokens=150 and add 'Answer in one sentence' to prevent the model from generating long, costly explanations you don't need.

techniques.name: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) Context Trimming
techniques.description: Retrieves and injects only the most relevant chunks via reranking rather than stuffing full documents, reducing input tokens and improving answer quality.
techniques.example: Use a reranker to select the top 3 passages instead of passing 20 retrieved chunks, cutting context from 8,000 to 1,500 tokens.

techniques.name: Request Batching
techniques.description: Groups multiple independent prompts into a single batch request (or uses provider batch APIs) to reduce overhead and unlock discounted asynchronous pricing.
techniques.savings: up to 50% reduction via batch API discounts
techniques.example: Submit 10,000 non-urgent classification jobs through OpenAI's Batch API to get results within 24 hours at 50% off standard rates.

techniques.name: Structured Output / Function Calling
techniques.description: Forces the model to return compact JSON or schema-constrained output, eliminating verbose prose and reducing both token usage and parsing errors.
techniques.example: Use OpenAI's structured outputs with a JSON schema so the model returns {"category":"billing"} instead of a paragraph explaining its reasoning.

techniques.name: Streaming with Early Termination
techniques.description: Streams responses and stops generation as soon as the needed information or a stop sequence is produced, avoiding paying for unused trailing tokens.
techniques.example: Define a stop sequence of '</answer>' so generation halts immediately once the answer tag closes rather than continuing to a token limit.

techniques.name: Fine-tuned Small Models for Repetitive Tasks
techniques.description: Replaces large-model calls for narrow, high-volume tasks with a small fine-tuned or open-source model, dramatically lowering per-call cost at inference.
techniques.example: Replace GPT-4o calls for intent classification with a fine-tuned Llama 3 8B model hosted on your own GPU for near-zero marginal cost.

tools.name: GPTCache
tools.description: Open-source semantic cache that stores LLM responses and serves them for similar queries using embedding similarity, cutting repeated API calls.
tools.pricing_paid: Free (open source); you pay only for underlying vector store/infra

tools.name: LiteLLM
tools.description: Unified proxy/SDK that routes requests across 100+ LLM providers with built-in caching, fallback routing, load balancing, and cost tracking.
tools.pricing_paid: Open-source free; LiteLLM Enterprise from ~$250/mo for SSO, support, and admin features

tools.name: Helicone
tools.description: LLM observability and gateway platform providing request logging, caching, cost monitoring, rate limiting, and prompt analytics.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier up to 10k requests/mo; paid plans from ~$20/mo and usage-based scaling

tools.name: Redis Semantic Cache
tools.description: Uses Redis vector search to cache and retrieve LLM responses by semantic similarity for low-latency, high-hit-rate caching.
tools.pricing_paid: Redis open-source free; Redis Cloud managed plans from ~$5/mo scaling with usage

tools.name: LangChain
tools.description: LLM application framework with built-in caching (in-memory, SQLite, Redis, semantic), prompt templating, and RAG tooling to reduce redundant calls.

tools.name: LLMLingua
tools.description: Microsoft's prompt compression toolkit that reduces prompt and context length up to 20x while retaining task performance.

tools.name: Portkey
tools.description: AI gateway offering semantic caching, smart routing, fallbacks, load balancing, and observability across multiple LLM providers.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier available; paid plans from ~$49/mo and enterprise pricing

tools.name: OpenRouter
tools.description: Unified API that routes to many models/providers with automatic price and availability-based routing to pick the cheapest viable model.
tools.pricing_paid: Free to use; pay per-token at provider rates plus small markup

quick_wins: Enable prompt caching by moving large static system prompts and few-shot examples to the start of every request for up to 90% off cached input tokens.
Switch default traffic to a cheaper model (e.g., GPT-4o-mini or Claude Haiku) and only escalate to a frontier model when needed.
Add semantic caching (GPTCache or Redis) in front of your LLM to serve repeated/similar queries without an API call.
Set sensible max_tokens limits and ask for concise or structured JSON output to cut expensive output tokens.
Route all non-urgent, high-volume jobs through provider Batch APIs for an immediate ~50% discount.
